(in fact, there's a movement to revive the worship of the pantheon today) It was the Byzantine Empire, emerging from the collapse of the Roman Empire, that brought Christianity to the Greeks, hence the similar sects of Greek Orthodox, Egyptian Orthodox (Coptic), and Russian Orthodox churches.

But, interestingly, the nature of Christianity owes something to the pre-Christian Greeks through its incorporation of elements of Platonism (the philosophy of Plato) In fact, Christianity is a product of a weird mix of near-east religions and philosophies that were vying for popularity across that whole region of the world during what is called the Hellenistic period of Greek history. (when Greece itself was in decline but still culturally influenced much of the world in the wake of the conquests of Alexander the Great, having rulers even in Egypt. The famed Cleopatra was Greek)

This cluster of religions--Judaism, Zoroastrianism, Gnosticism, Platonism--all share concepts, language, and names for things interchangeably and all contributed basic concepts to Christianity--as well as Islam. (people don't realize the close relationship. The Koran talks about the Virgin Mary more than the Bible does!) Judaism gave it the saga of the Old Testament and the 'model' for god. Zoroastrianism gave it the idea of dualism as an eternal conflict between darkness and light. Gnosticism gave it the concept of dualism as upper and lower realms of existence and god as this compound being with different aspects, and Platonism gave it the notion of divine cosmological order.

To give you an idea of how all this mixes together in interesting ways, in Gnosticism there's this idea that there's a 'real' god in heaven but a lesser god that rules over the physical world --a 'demiurge'. And this demiurge was born of one of god's rogue aspects--the seven archons--named Sophia, who is the only female archon and also associated with the Greek/Roman Aphrodite/Venus. She's one of the 'classical' planets --the ones we could see with the naked eye. The archons are all named for those planets. The archons are avatars or aspects of the real god, created to give him the ability to interface to the universe. And they all represent various aspects of god's personality. But they also express their own personalities, which are sometimes inclined for good and sometimes evil and which gets them into trouble. It's from this that Christianity get the 'archangels' and 'archdemons', seven of each, with names linguistically relating to the archons' names.

So, as one Gnostic myth goes, Sophia is exploring in the lower realms of the proto-creation, which is a bit dangerous because the more archons move away from the light of god the more muddled their thinking gets. And this results in her getting the idea that she would like to create things herself just like god does, but she doesn't know quite how. Somehow, she causes herself to become pregnant and gives birth to a monstrosity and is so horrified by what she's created that she pukes up the physical world as we know it and abandons her creation. Her monstrous child then grows up alone in this new world thinking he's the god of all that's around him. And what's his name? Yahweh.

And the themes of these myths keep playing out in western culture in all sorts of curious ways. The demonology in so many fantasy games and literature derive from these old religions. Like in Blizzard's Diablo series. It's all this stuff deriving from or referencing Gnosticism and Zoroastrianism. Eternal war between light and dark. Seven archangels and archdemons. A midrealm between heaven and hell created by rogue angels and demons. Humankind created from their union in an attempt to end the eternal war.
